title: Quant Market Brief — October 22, 2026: Inference Shift & AI-Capex Risk

stories.headline: Conformal guarantees can fail when inference configuration changes
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Doula & Mühlhäuser, arXiv 2610.28937v1, submitted October 20, 2026; accepted NeurIPS 2026. Conceptual audit diagram.
stories.alt: Two boxes compare calibration under one inference configuration with deployment under another, feeding an exchangeability-risk warning. The image does not invent coverage values.
stories.fact: A NeurIPS 2026 paper evaluates conformal prediction across eight language models, four finite-label benchmarks and 12 inference configurations. The authors find that changing inference settings such as quantization or temperature can shift score distributions and make matched calibration substantially overstate deployment coverage.
stories.inference: Serving configuration is part of the statistical data-generating process even when model weights and task data are unchanged.
stories.uncertainty: This is one accepted research study, not a universal failure rate. Coverage loss is heterogeneous across models and datasets, and the abstract does not provide one portable correction factor.
stories.why: Treat quantization, decoding temperature and runtime policy as versioned calibration inputs. Recalibrate—or at least run coverage audits—after serving changes before trusting uncertainty gates.
stories.short: Conformal coverage can deteriorate when deployment changes temperature, quantization or other inference settings. Version the serving stack and audit coverage after every such change.

stories.headline: State-space LOB model learns a steerable representation of market dynamics
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Mohl et al., arXiv 2610.28753v1, submitted October 20, 2026; accepted ICAIF 2026. R² is author-reported.
stories.alt: A bar shows reported order-flow-imbalance decoder R squared near 0.59 beside boxes for internal market state, transfer to unseen stocks and a feature-axis steering test.
stories.fact: The authors trained an 8.2-million-parameter Mamba-3 model on tokenized messages from eight large-cap U.S. equities. Order-flow imbalance was decodable from the learned state at approximately R² 0.59; reported transfer extended to unseen stocks and other measures including volume and volatility.
stories.inference: The model may be learning a reusable microstructure state rather than only memorizing ticker-specific message patterns.
stories.uncertainty: The results are author-reported and require independent replication. Decodability and causal steering do not establish realistic fills, market impact or profitable trading.
stories.why: Add representation probes to simulator validation, but keep execution realism separate: test impact, queue position, cancellation latency and cross-regime transfer before using the model for policy training.
stories.short: A Mamba-3 LOB model reportedly encodes order-flow imbalance at R²≈0.59 and transfers to unseen stocks. Useful representation evidence is not yet proof of execution realism.

stories.headline: Nasdaq futures fall 1.9% as AI-cost concerns and oil shock hit risk appetite
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Reuters/LSEG snapshot at 4:56 a.m. ET on October 22, 2026. Indicative futures—not cash-market returns.
stories.alt: Horizontal bars show Dow e-mini minus 0.69 percent, S&P 500 e-mini minus 1.10 percent and Nasdaq-100 e-mini minus 1.93 percent, with a caption noting higher oil, lower yields and a higher VIX.
stories.fact: At 4:56 a.m. ET, Reuters reported Dow e-minis −0.69%, S&P 500 e-minis −1.10% and Nasdaq-100 e-minis −1.93%. Brent was up more than 3% near $112, while the 10-year Treasury yield was around 5.085%; Meta, Tesla and major chip shares were lower premarket.
stories.inference: The early move combined duration-sensitive AI-capex repricing with an inflationary oil shock, concentrating downside in technology.
stories.uncertainty: Futures are indicative and can reverse before or after the cash open. Consolidated ETF spreads, displayed depth, auction imbalances and options gamma were not reliably available at the cutoff.
stories.why: Avoid extrapolating the futures move into market orders. Refresh ES/NQ–SPY/QQQ basis, NBBO depth, quote age and opening imbalance; use bounded limits and smaller participation until books stabilize.
stories.short: At 4:56 a.m. ET, Nasdaq-100 futures were −1.93% versus S&P −1.10% and Dow −0.69%, with Brent near $112. Treat the signal as indicative and reprice execution at the open.

stories.headline: September pending-home sales drop 7.3% across all U.S. regions
stories.credit: Market State Lab; National Association of Realtors, released October 20, 2026. Signed-contract indicator; financing and closing outcomes remain uncertain.
stories.alt: Horizontal bars show September monthly pending-home-sales declines in the Northeast, Midwest, South, West and nationally; every value is negative and the national change is minus 7.3 percent.
stories.fact: NAR reported pending-home sales fell 7.3% from August and 11.3% from a year earlier in September. All four regions declined monthly: Northeast −4.2%, Midwest −6.5%, South −8.2% and West −9.2%.
stories.inference: High borrowing costs are suppressing housing demand even before signed contracts convert into closings, reinforcing rate sensitivity outside AI-led investment.
stories.uncertainty: This is an industry association series based on contracts, not completed sales. Financing, appraisal and inspection failures can alter the mapping to final closings, and later revisions are possible.
stories.why: Use the release as a leading housing feature with publication timestamps and vintages. Pair it with mortgage rates and applications; do not treat one monthly print as a direct Fed decision rule.
stories.short: Pending-home sales fell 7.3% month over month and 11.3% year over year, with declines in all regions. It is a leading contract indicator, not a completed-sales measure.

stories.headline: Meta couples strong revenue with heavier AI financing and negative free cash flow
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Reuters, October 21–22, 2026. Quarterly revenue/free cash flow and full-year capex forecast are shown on separate visual elements.
stories.alt: A two-bar chart shows Meta third-quarter revenue of 64.6 billion dollars and negative free cash flow of 2.12 billion dollars, beside a separate box showing a full-year capital-expenditure forecast range of 135 to 145 billion dollars.
stories.fact: Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion and said Muse surpassed 10 million users in the U.S. and Canada. Reuters reported negative quarterly free cash flow of $2.12 billion, a 2026 capital-spending forecast of $135–145 billion and a planned new non-voting share class to help fund AI investment.
stories.inference: User adoption is scaling faster than near-term cash generation, making financing structure and capital efficiency central to the AI thesis.
stories.uncertainty: Muse monetization is prospective, the new shares are planned rather than already issued, and legal liabilities add uncertainty. Strong revenue does not prove acceptable returns on AI capital.
stories.why: For tech-factor models, separate demand indicators from capital intensity. Track revenue, free cash flow, capex revisions and financing actions as distinct state variables rather than collapsing them into a single “AI growth” signal.
stories.short: Meta posted $64.6bn quarterly revenue and Muse adoption above 10m users, but free cash flow turned negative and 2026 capex guidance reached $135–145bn. Growth and capital intensity must be modeled separately.
